Anyone who can rewrite a chunk can rewrite its checksum.' and #not-implemented 'Authenticity. CRC-32C is not a signature.' The operational consequence for a game that loads downloaded or modded .cnb files (own signature/trusted transport) is not stated, while deep-dives/content/cnj-documents.html#limits advises 'for content from untrusted sources, compile to CNB', which a reader can take as a safety statement about provenance.

fix.old_html: • Not tamper-proof. The checksums detect accidental corruption. Anyone who can rewrite a chunk can rewrite its checksum.
fix.html: • Not tamper-proof. The checksums detect accidental corruption. Anyone who can rewrite a chunk can rewrite its checksum, so a game that loads .cnb files from untrusted downloads or mods needs its own signature or trusted-transport policy; the bounded, validated parse protects the loader from malformed input, not from a forged but well-formed file.

findings.bible: Container contract: 'Overflow, overlap, duplicate singleton chunks, invalid UTF-8, unknown required chunks and resource limits are rejected before a runtime object is constructed.'
findings.target: modules/content/src/Cnb/CnbDocument.cpp::CnbDocument::FindSingle (throws "has N 'XXXX' chunks, but this schema allows at most one") and ::RequireSingle (throws "is missing its required 'XXXX' chunk"); every built-in codec opens its header and data chunks through them (CnbCurveCodec, CnbTextureCodec, CnbSoundEffectCodec, CnbModelCodec ...), so the check runs before any runtime object is built.
findings.site_now: docs/cnb-format.html#layout-invariants lists the Parse() invariants (ascending offsets, exact tiling, zero-length chunks, overflow-checked arithmetic, CRC, exact expansion); #chunks says CMET and XREF appear at most once. Nothing says that a duplicated or missing schema chunk is refused, so a hand-written or third-party writer has no stated multiplicity rule.

fix.old_html: • A compressed chunk expands to exactly its declared uncompressedSize.
fix.html:
• A compressed chunk expands to exactly its declared uncompressedSize.

    • Chunk multiplicity is a schema rule, checked by the schema decoder after Parse() rather than by it: a chunk type that a schema allows only once (for example TEXH or CRVH) but that appears twice is refused (“has N ‘XXXX’ chunks, but this schema allows at most one”), and so is a required one that is missing (“is missing its required ‘XXXX’ chunk”). A custom schema gets the same checks from CnbDocument::FindSingle() and RequireSingle().

findings.bible: Schemas and asset families: 'Each schema has a producer and runtime loader; schema IDs and chunk IDs are frozen independently of C++ enum order.'
findings.target: modules/content/include/CNA/Content/Cnb/CnbTextureFormat.hpp::CnbTextureFormat (doc comment: SurfaceFormat's enumerators are numbered by position, so serializing them would let inserting an enumerator renumber every .cnb; the CNB values are frozen, written explicitly, and mapped by CnbTextureFormatToSurfaceFormat / SurfaceFormatToCnbTextureFormat, which must be edited deliberately); CnbFormat.hpp::CnbAssetTypeId are explicit constants and chunk ids are MakeChunkId(a,b,c,d) characters.
findings.site_now: docs/cnb-format.html#asset-types says only 'The numeric values of the built-in types are frozen'; #compression says codec ids are frozen; the rule that no on-disk identifier follows a runtime enum's declaration order, and why texture format ids are a separate enum, is absent, so a maintainer extending SurfaceFormat has no warning that the CNB mapping is a separate deliberate step.

fix.old_html: The header's assetTypeId selects the schema and the loader. The numeric values of the built-in types are frozen.
fix.html: The header's assetTypeId selects the schema and the loader. The numeric values of the built-in types are frozen. They are explicit constants, not the position of an enumerator in a runtime type, and the same holds for the other identifiers a file stores: chunk identifiers are four ASCII bytes, and texture format ids are their own CnbTextureFormat values, mapped to and from SurfaceFormat by the explicit functions CnbTextureFormatToSurfaceFormat() and SurfaceFormatToCnbTextureFormat(), because SurfaceFormat is numbered by position and inserting an enumerator would otherwise renumber every file already written. Changing a runtime enum therefore never changes the format; changing that mapping is a deliberate edit.

The contract is that no PROCESS failure can leave a partial file where a complete one was'); used by tools/content/content.cpp via WriteFileAtomically.
findings.site_now: docs/content-pipeline.html#incremental-builds: 'Each output is written to a temporary sibling and renamed over the destination, so an interrupted build leaves the old file or the new file, never a prefix of the new one.' States the guarantee for any interruption; the TARGET contract covers process failure only (no fsync, so power loss or an OS crash is outside it) and rests on a platform-specific replace primitive. development/internals/content/pipeline.html#publication does not carry the caveat either.

fix.old_html: • Atomic publication. Each output is written to a temporary sibling and renamed over the destination, so an interrupted build leaves the old file or the new file, never a prefix of the new one.
fix.html: • Atomic publication. Each output is written to a temporary sibling and renamed over the destination (a replacing rename on POSIX, MoveFileExW with replace-existing on Windows), so a build whose process is killed or fails leaves the old file or the new file, never a prefix of the new one. Nothing is fsynced, so power loss or an operating-system crash is outside that guarantee.

fix.html:
The statements in this section describe evidence CNA publishes about itself at this snapshot. The site did not re-run the oracle or the interop harness; treat them as CNA's claims with the scope stated.

Build success is not runtime proof. A produced asset must still be loaded, and graphics or audio content must be engaged on the renderer or device route you ship: an Effect, for instance, is written to .xnb on any host but loads only where the active renderer reports the CompiledEffects capability.
